contributions.statement: Before trusting an agent-built component that passes its own tests, run a randomized differential campaign against an independent reference; in one agent-built compiler 82% of random inputs exposed defects, concentrated in unverified text interfaces and the spec-vs-hardware boundary.
contributions.evidence: §V-B: first 30-minute detect phase, 6,760 of 8,200 generated programs triggered a defect; after 5 repairs a second 4,600-program phase surfaced none. Single artifact by the same author.

contributions.statement: Accept an agent's repair only after a fresh detect window on newly generated, unseen inputs stays clean, as a check against fixes tailored to the failing cases.
contributions.evidence: §I Reward Hacking, §V: repeated detect-repair-revalidate rounds until clean windows; reward-hacking absence judged only by the author, failed/escalated attempts excluded from reporting.

reason: Lean compilers are far from Java services, but the measured defect rate of an agent-built, self-tested artifact under randomized differential testing is a usable constraint; the rest is known test practice.
